payloads.description: Establish baseline authenticated behavior and capture session tokens/cookies from successful login if any
High-confidence auth bypass probes (SQL-like tautologies) to detect authentication bypass or error leakage
Null-byte pair to trigger parsing differences if earlier probes indicate anomalies

prerequisites.description: Run without Cookies/Authorization to observe baseline; if successful login needed, capture Set-Cookie or Authorization from benign step
prerequisites.custom_logic: If benign login returns auth token/cookie, bind it for downstream tests. Abort further auth-probe attempts if account lockout detected in responses.

prerequisites.description: If CSRF required, fetch /login GET before POST and extract token named csrf or X-CSRF-Token

oracle_rules.condition: Compare probe/exploit responses to benign baseline. Trigger if status code becomes one of [200,302] when baseline is not, or body length changes by >=20%
Detect authentication error messages, stack traces, SQL/NoSQL driver keywords in probe/exploit responses not present in baseline

test_cases.notes: Primary authentication staging. Capture auth artifacts for use by subsequent tests. Stop if lockout or WAF blocks observed (403/429 signatures).

payloads.description: Create a controlled test account using unique timestamped email to enable downstream authenticated tests. Replace {{ts}} at runtime.
Probe NoSQL/SQL operator injection in email and password fields to detect parsing errors or acceptance anomalies
Exploit-tier crafted inputs for parsing errors; use unique emails to avoid creating real admin accounts

prerequisites.description: Ensure low-volume account creation only. Use unique timestamps and stop further register tests on successful creation to avoid pollution
prerequisites.custom_logic: If account created, capture credentials and token for downstream authenticated tests; cease additional registration probes to respect safety.

prerequisites.description: If CSRF required, fetch /register GET and extract token

oracle_rules.condition: Detect NoSQL/DB/driver error keywords or stack traces in probe/exploit responses compared to baseline
If response code differs from baseline or body length changes by >=30% for probe/exploit, flag potential parsing/execution issues

test_cases.notes: Register only enough accounts to supply two controlled accounts for authorization tests; prioritize creating one account then reuse for login in PLAN-001 if needed.

payloads.description: Collect tokens and cookies from prior PLAN-001 and PLAN-002 runs and bind them to header:Cookie and header:Authorization for subsequent tests

prerequisites.description: Requires successful login from PLAN-001 benign step or account created in PLAN-002 then logged in
prerequisites.extract_from: /login POST response headers or body or /register then /login
prerequisites.custom_logic: Prefer Cookie if Set-Cookie observed; prefer Authorization header if JSON token observed. Also capture CSRF tokens from GET responses when present.

test_cases.notes: Mandatory setup stage to ensure downstream tests run with correct authenticated context. If tokens absent, set needs_observation=true and abort dependent tests.

payloads.description: Fetch each resource with primary test account token to establish baseline JSON metadata sizes and fields
For each resource perform a single comparison request using second controlled account token (or modified token if token format alteration previously indicated) to detect IDOR/authorization bypass
If token manipulation allowed and safe (observed in PLAN-001/003), perform one controlled token modification per resource to test altered owner-id access (no iteration)

prerequisites.description: Authenticated tokens for two controlled accounts obtained and bound via PLAN-003
prerequisites.bind_to: header:Cookie and header:Cookie:other_user_session or header:Authorization and header:Authorization:other
prerequisites.custom_logic: Do not attempt to enumerate user IDs; only perform single comparison per endpoint.

oracle_rules.condition: If other-user or modified-token request returns 200 where baseline expected 401/403, flag authorization bypass
If other-user response body length differs by >=30-50% (endpoint dependent) indicating additional data exposure, flag sensitive data exposure

test_cases.notes: Prioritize endpoints returning sensitive data (all_users, total_money) first. Capture only indicators (status, sizes, fields) not full sensitive payloads. Stop token-modification attempts if any sign of privilege escalation or unexpected admin-level data.
